summary: E1.5 'Seguir trabajando' bug NOT fully fixed. Backend pytest (18/18 workspace tests) PASS and curl items 1-4 PASS in isolation, but the live E2E from the frontend produces HTTP 500 → 'Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)' shown under the button. RCA confirmed: the fix that swapped block_id from server-generated to client-supplied (b.id) collides with the unique index on workspace_blocks.block_id, causing pymongo.errors.BulkWriteError E11000. The traceback also exposes a secondary bug in the global exception handler (the BulkWriteError contains BSON bytes that crash JSONResponse render, producing the unhelpful bare 500). Tests 5,6 BLOCKED by the 500; test 7 (team share) PASS via curl.

critical.issue: DuplicateKeyError E11000 on workspace_blocks.block_id_1 when the client re-uses an ephemeral block id across sessions (e.g. 'blk_h1'). After the E1.5 fix `block_id` is persisted from `b.id` (client) instead of `new_block_id()` (server), but Mongo enforces a global UNIQUE index on `block_id` alone. Every 2nd 'Seguir trabajando' from any browser session that emits the same client id returns 500.

critical.endpoint: global exception handler (src/core/exceptions.py / starlette base middleware)
critical.issue: Uncaught exceptions whose repr/args contain bytes (BSON Binary, ObjectId raw, DuplicateKeyError details) crash the default 500 renderer with 'TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable', leaking a bare 'Internal Server Error' to the client. Add a catch-all handler that returns a sanitized JSON 500 (and consider catching BulkWriteError / DuplicateKeyError specifically and translating to 409).

integration_issues.issue: Button surfaces 'Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)' under the button instead of navigating. The router.push('/w/${workspaceId}') change is correct, but never executes because promoteToWorkspace() throws ApiError 500 first.

action_items: FIX #1 (root cause of the live 500): make block_id unique per workspace, NOT globally. Either (a) drop the unique index on `block_id` alone and add compound unique `(workspace_id, block_id)`, OR (b) persist a server-side `block_id = new_block_id()` for storage and keep `client_block_id = b.id` as a non-unique echo field, returning `client_block_id` as `block_id` in GET responses, OR (c) namespace storage id as `f'{workspace_id}:{b.id}'`. Then re-test from the frontend: the same client ids must work across many promotions.

FIX #2 (secondary, ergonomic): in the global error path, catch pymongo BulkWriteError / DuplicateKeyError and return 409 with a JSON-safe body. Also harden the catch-all 500 renderer to coerce non-serializable values to repr(...) so we never leak a bare 'Internal Server Error'.

FIX #3 (test gap): add a backend regression that creates two workspaces back-to-back from the same user with overlapping `b.id` values — this would have caught the live bug. Current `test_create_workspace_round_trips_block_id` only creates ONE workspace.

FIX #4 (test gap): the Playwright frontend test added (open-workspace-button.test.tsx) probably mocks the API and so missed the duplicate-key path. Add an integration test that actually POSTs to /api/workspaces twice with the same client ids.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend src/modules/workspaces/service.py:244 — `'block_id': b.id` violates the global UNIQUE index on block_id. Either the index assumption or this line must change.

Backend src/core/exceptions.py:43 — there is no `@app.exception_handler(Exception)` catch-all that produces a JSON 500. Any uncaught exception whose args contain bytes (very common with pymongo) yields the misleading TypeError chain and a plain-text 500 — this masked the real bug for the test that 'passed' isolated.
Frontend OpenWorkspaceButton.tsx:41 — `router.push('/w/${workspaceId}')` correct, surfaces ApiError detail+status. Code is fine; it just never gets to push because the API errors first.

Frontend CopilotProvider.tsx:338-344 — `b.id` is taken from the in-memory block; if the renderer assigns deterministic short ids (e.g. `blk_hero_<n>`), they will collide across sessions. This is the root user-visible symptom.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce instantly with: curl -X POST <BASE>/api/workspaces -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -b cookies -d '{"ephemeral_state":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"},{"role":"assistant","content":"y"}],"blocks":[{"id":"blk_h1","type":"hero","props":{}}]},"workspace_type":"analyze","title":null,"organization_id":"org_a720ff5087aa"}' → 500. mongosh shows `db.workspace_blocks.getIndexes()` includes `{key:{block_id:1}, unique:true}`. Real Mongo error visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log: E11000 duplicate key error collection: arroba_com.workspace_blocks index: block_id_1.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: arroba_com.workspace_blocks has a UNIQUE index on `block_id` alone. The E1.5 fix changed `service.create_workspace` to persist `block_id = b.id` (client-supplied) instead of `new_block_id()`. Client-supplied ids are NOT globally unique (frontend reuses them: e.g. 'blk_h1' on every promotion), so the second and subsequent inserts raise pymongo.errors.BulkWriteError E11000. The exception is not handled, the default 500 path tries to JSON-serialize the BulkWriteError details which contain ObjectId/datetime/bytes in BSON form, triggering 'TypeError: Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable'. The client sees an opaque 'Internal Server Error (HTTP 500)' and the user's URL stays at /es (well actually at /organizaciones) because router.push never runs. REPRODUCTION STEPS: (1) login buyer, (2) open dock, (3) Analiza Kitchen Studio, (4) click Seguir trabajando. MITIGATION: change unique index to compound (workspace_id, block_id) — this preserves the idempotency intent (sent id == returned id within a workspace) without colliding across workspaces. Also add a global exception handler and a DuplicateKeyError handler.
